text:
eli: flagging a subtle bug: when we route overflow traffic to the cost-tier fallback, the sampler runs twice (ingress + fallback) and occasionally the fallback sample wins, which means the console can show unredacted values for entries we thought were redacted upstream. Need a policy decision on invariant enforcement.

priya: yikes. is this a race or a config mismatch? can you paste a short repro (sanitized)?

eli: sanitized: 
```
ingress: route=/v1/embeddings tenant=t-88 sampled_out (redacted)
fallback: route=/v1/embeddings-fallback tenant=t-88 sampled_in (raw.user_id=joe@corp)
```
The console merges the two and shows raw.user_id.

kevin: root cause: sampler_id is per-service. When requests are proxied to fallback the header sampler-decisions are dropped and fallback re-evaluates. Two practical fixes: 1) canonicalize sampler-decision header and treat it as authoritative downstream OR 2) enforce a strict downstream redact-once rule where any incoming request with a prior-sampled tag forces `remove` semantics.

sam: option 1 is cleaner for observability (we keep original decision) but option 2 is safer for privacy (prevents downstream accidental reveals). I vote for option 2 as default with an opt-in override for enterprise tenants that want more debugability.

leah: UX angle: console should never show raw PII coming from sampled records unless explicit unseal/audit flow happened. So we must ensure the UI honors a `redaction_state` on the merged trace. If any ancestor segment is redacted, the merged view stays redacted.

priya: agree. Let's define a contract: sampler emits a single header `x-rw-sample-state` = one of `kept`, `redacted:level=<none|pseudonym|sealed>`, `dropped`. Downstream services must not overwrite `redacted:*` with `kept`. They may append `;via=service-name` but not change level.

kevin: technical note: `sealed` means we created an audit blob id and stored sealed payload in KMS. `pseudonym` = stable per-tenant HMAC. `none` = raw (should be disallowed for sampled). We should map old headers to the new format in the edge.

sam: implementation plan: sampler runtime adds canonical header. Proxy (mux) preserves header on routing and refuses to forward request to fallback without the header. Fallback will apply `remove` if header absent. Also add an assert in dev-mode to catch services that clobber header.

eli: what about async writers that create sealed blobs later? The sampler may mark `redacted:sealed;pending` and update the sample record when blob ready. Console shows pseudonym until sealed completes. If unseal requested before sealed, show "unseal pending".

leah: dashboard requests: show per-route metric "merged-redaction-leak-rate" (cases where merged view would have raw values). Also a column for "avg-seal-latency(s)" and "pct-samples-without-canonical-header". Product wants SLA before enabling on large tenants.

kevin: billing/storage: sealed blobs billed per-GB-month; default retention 90d. Provide tenant opt-out which forces `redacted:pseudonym` or `redacted:remove`. Default for new tenants = `pseudonym` with no sealed blobs unless explicitly enabled.

priya: rollout: enforce header and fallback-as-remove behind feature flag. Canary on 3% tenants for 48h, measure merged-redaction-leak-rate -> must be 0. Then open to 20% and region roll.

sam: perf note: adding header is cheap. Creating HMAC pseudonym per sampled value small CPU hit; async sealing job is the cost. Expect ~1.2% CPU uptick during canary.

eli: ops-bot: please schedule canary once RFC is up.

ops-bot: deploy-bot: sampler-canonical-headers v1 scheduled to canary in eng-platform on 2024-10-02T03:00:00Z (auto).

priya: action items: 1) RFC for canonical header + contract (pri). 2) implement sampler header emission + edge mapping (sam). 3) proxy preserve/assert behavior (kevin). 4) console merge logic + banner for pending seals (leah). 5) telemetry columns and alerts (eli). 6) canary plan + billing notes (priya).

kevin: +1. I'll prepare migration adapter for older services.

leah: will prototype UI banner states this afternoon.

sam: starting on PR for header emission and async seal state machine.

priya: thanks, will file RFC and tag legal for retention policy. No objections -> moving forward.
